name: Conics-1-tangents and normals
questiontext:
Find the equations of the tangent and normal to the circle \[ {{CT:0}}\] at the point \(({{CT:1}},{{CT:2}})\).

Tangent: [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

Normal: [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]]
generalfeedback:
Tangents: Circles are a special case of the ellipse centred at \((x_c,y_c)\)
\[ \frac{(x-x_c)^2}{a^2}+\frac{(y-y_c)^2}{b^2}=1.\]
The tangent to this ellipse, through the point \((x',y')\), is given by
\[ \frac{(x-x_c)(x'-x_c)}{a^2}+\frac{(y-y_c)(y'-y_c)}{b^2}=1.\]
In our case we have \(a^2=b^2={{CT:3}}\) and \(x'={{CT:1}}\) and \(y'={{CT:2}}\). Using these values we have
the tangent line as
\[ {{CT:4}}\]
Expanding and rearranging give
\[ {{CT:5}}\]

Normals: A line through \((x',y')\) with gradient \(m\) has equation \[ y=m(x-x')+y'.\] If a line has gradient \(m\) then the perpendicular line has gradient \(-1/m\). Our tangent line has gradient {{CT:6}}, so the normal line through \(({{CT:1}},{{CT:2}})\) has equation \[ y= {{CT:7}} = {{CT:8}}.\]

on_true.feedback: The equation for your tangent is correct.

on_false.feedback: The equation for your tangent is incorrect.

on_true.feedback: The equation for your normal is correct.

on_false.feedback: The equation for your normal is incorrect.
